newsitem.title: UK: UK tobacco industry fuming over tax rise.
newsitem.headline: UK tobacco industry fuming over tax rise.

text.p: Britain's Tobacco Alliance, the lobby group for independent retailers of tobacco, reacted angrily on Tuesday to the increase in tax on both hand rolling tobacco and cigarettes in the Chancellor's budget statement.

"The black market trade in tobacco is flourishing. Does the Chancellor not know that with each tobacco tax increase tobacco smuggling increases and organised crime increases?" said Paul Mason, spokesman for the Alliance in a statement.
Clarke said that from 1800 GMT tonight the tax on a packet of 20 cigarettes would rise by about 15p, on a packet of small cigars by some 7p and on a packet of pipe tobacco by about 8p.

But Clarke limited the increase in duty on hand rolling tobacco to the rate of inflation because he said it is "proving by far the easiest tobacco product to smuggle, although it does represent a very small part of the total tobacco market."
A 50 gramme pack of hand rolling tobacco normally costs about 7.47 stg in Britain by can be bought for slightly under 2.0 stg in Belgium.
The Tobacco Council estimate 68 percent of all hand rolling tobacco sold in Britain comes from mainland Europe and some 62 perecnt of that is smuggled.
Shares in Imperial Tobacco, whose brands include John Player Special, Embassy and Panama cigars, were off 4p at 371p.
However, the tax increases were greeted favourably by anti-smoking lobby group ASH.
"By increasing the price by 15p, approximately 2,700 lives will be saved in the long run as a result of the expected fall in consumption," ASH spokeswoman Karen Williams said in a statement.
